q: We introduce SWE-WebDev Bench, an evaluation framework designed to answer this question
r: Include: new 68-metric benchmark evaluating AI app builders on project-level web application building from business requirements.

q: The builder-finder split separates implementation ability from artifact recovery while exposing interactions between artifacts and inspection policies.
r: Include: new evaluation protocol for agent-built repositories with repeated trials across models and reasoning efforts.

q: SWE-CHAIN: We introduce the first benchmark for chained release-level maintenance
r: Include: new benchmark of release-level upgrades from natural-language specifications, feature-level evaluation method, not issue repair.

q: ROADMAPBENCH introduces a new evaluation axis for coding agents: multi-target, long-horizon software development across real version upgrades.
r: Include: new benchmark with a Completion Score for feature-level, multi-file development tasks from roadmap specifications.

q: We introduced WebGameBench, a requirement-to-application benchmark for coding agents based on browser-native games.
r: Include: new requirement-to-application benchmark in which agents build whole applications from a specification.

q: We propose ProcCtrlBench, a benchmark for execution-process evaluation in LLM coding agents beyond final outcomes.
r: Include: main contribution is a process-level evaluation method (defect ontology, control-preservation metrics) comparing agent-model systems; borderline since cases come partly from SWE-bench-Verified.

q: We introduced EVOCODE-BENCH, a benchmark for persistent multi-turn coding with cumulative tests, stateful workspaces, and round-level diagnostics.
r: Include: new benchmark with four attempts per task, feature-level iterative building and evolving requirements.

q: A Figma-to-full-stack benchmark for Web and Mobile.
r: Include: new benchmark where agents build full-stack applications from design handoffs and requirements, with trace analysis.

q: We present Asuka-Bench, the first web generation benchmark that systematically evaluates code agents
r: Include: new benchmark for web project generation under underspecified requirements with multi-round refinement, comparing models and agent frameworks.

q: We take the position that current coding benchmarks are misaligned with agentic software engineering
r: Include: peer-style full-length position paper on how coding agents are evaluated (harness, context files, reference solutions), relevant to RQ3; not an editorial or keynote.
